script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. SUBURBAN NEIGHBORHOOD - DAY

We open on a peaceful suburban neighborhood. Children play in the streets. Lawns are lush and green. Birds chirp in the trees. A perfect day.

INT. KITCHEN - JENNY'S HOUSE - DAY

JENNY (30s, an introverted woman) stands in her kitchen, staring at a family photo. She is surrounded by ingredients for dinner. A knock at the door startles her.

JENNY
(calling out)
Come in.

The door opens, revealing her EX-HUSBAND, MIKE (30s, a charming but restless man).

MIKE
(surprised)
Hey, Jenny. I didn't know you were home.

JENNY
(hesitant)
What can I do for you, Mike?

MIKE
(awkward pause)
Well, I was wondering if we could talk about the kids. About how we're raising them.

JENNY
(defensive)
I think we've covered that ground before.

MIKE
(apologetic)
I know, I know. But things have changed for me. I've been doing a lot of thinking.

JENNY
(sighs)
What's changed?

MIKE
I've been traveling a lot for work. And I've realized that I want to be more involved in our children's lives. I want to be the kind of father I should have been before.

JENNY
(stern)
That's all well and good, Mike. But I've been doing this alone for a long time. I've figured out how to raise our kids on my own. I don't need your input.

MIKE
(pleading)
Jenny, please. I know I've made mistakes in the past. But I want to make things right. I want to be a part of our children's lives again. Can't we at least try to work together on this?

JENNY
(sighs)
Fine. We can discuss it. But I'm not making any promises.

INT. DINNER TABLE - JENNY'S HOUSE - NIGHT

Jenny, Mike, and their children, SAM (10) and EMMA (8), sit around the dinner table. The atmosphere is tense.

JENNY
(looking at Mike)
So, Mike, what do you have to say about how we're raising the kids?

MIKE
(nervous)
Well, I've been thinking about their activities. I think they should try new things. Maybe sports or music.

JENNY
(rolls her eyes)
Here we go. I've already signed them up for soccer and piano lessons.

MIKE
(defensive)
I didn't know that. I just thought they could use more enrichment.

JENNY
(sighs)
Look, I appreciate your concern. But I've got this covered.

INT. SCHOOL PLAYGROUND - DAY

Jenny watches as Mike coaches Sam in a soccer game. Emma plays the piano for a school talent show. Jenny feels a pang of guilt for not allowing Mike to be more involved in their lives.

INT. KITCHEN - JENNY'S HOUSE - NIGHT

Jenny and Mike sit at the kitchen table, discussing their children.

JENNY
(apologetic)
I'm sorry, Mike. I've been holding on to old resentments. I know that's not fair to the kids.

MIKE
(forgiving)
It's okay, Jenny. We all make mistakes. But we can learn from them.

JENNY
(smiling)
You're right. Maybe it's time for us to work together on this.

MIKE
(relieved)
That's all I've ever wanted.

INT. FAMILY ROOM - JENNY'S HOUSE - EVENING

The family gathers in the family room to watch a movie. Jenny looks at Mike, feeling grateful for his presence in their lives.

MIKE
(whispering to Jenny)
I'm glad we're doing this.

JENNY
(smiling back)
Me too.

INT. BEDROOM - JENNY'S HOUSE - NIGHT

Jenny sits on the edge of the bed, staring at a photo of her family. She feels a sense of peace and contentment.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
And so, Jenny and Mike learned that the most important thing in life is not to hold on to the past, but to work together in the present, to raise their children as a team, and to discover the true meaning of identity as a family.

FADE OUT.

END OF SCREENPLAY.
